title: Color Overview
slide_intent: Show palette hierarchy alongside color definitions because recognition depends on both consistent hues and their relative roles.
strategic_value: Food-derived colors can connect Burger King packaging, marketing and interiors to ingredients and flame grilling.
demonstration: Six named color fields have different areas: red, orange and brown dominate, followed by Mayo Egg White and smaller stacked green/yellow blocks, all with printed production values.
practical_value: Read the fields as a qualitative order of importance and use the supplied specifications without inventing usage percentages.

content_islands.name: Palette rationale
content_islands.spec: Place the hierarchy and food-origin explanation inside the red field at left.

content_islands.name: Primary fields
content_islands.spec: Run red, orange and brown as three broad vertical fields, each with its specification near the bottom.

content_islands.name: Supporting fields
content_islands.spec: Place a narrower pale field then stacked green and yellow blocks at right, retaining each color name and values.

reference_purposes.Intent: The source explicitly connects the palette to fresh Whopper ingredients and flame grilling.
reference_purposes.Expression: Unequal color areas communicate a warm palette with smaller green and yellow accents.
reference_purposes.Application: The page supplies Pantone coated/uncoated, HEX, RGB and CMYK values and states that the palette is weighted by importance.

ingredient.name: Weighted color palette
ingredient.role: Connect the identity to food while keeping primary hues prominent.
ingredient.application: Use the stated palette and its qualitative order of importance; do not infer numeric proportions from field widths.
ingredient.scope: Historical guide. Fiery Red prints HEX #D62300 but R215 G35 B0; the red-channel values disagree by one. Preserve the source discrepancy rather than silently correcting it.
